Serial constraints cleared: lane in-flight 0 at round open. Co-dispatched: **#4820 + #5380** (config/guard files) and **#5174** batch 2 (`content/docs/**`, `scripts/check-doc-snippet-types.mjs`) — all disjoint from `README.md`. No in-flight PR touches the README.

## ⚠️ The card's blocker is already resolved — ⛔ do not re-investigate it

This card says its fork *"cannot be settled from inside the checkout; it needs the repository's Security settings."* **It can be, and the PM did.** Do not spend a step on it:

`list_workflows` for this repo returns **31** registered workflows. Four are `dynamic/*`:

- `dynamic/copilot-swe-agent/copilot`
- `dynamic/copilot-pull-request-reviewer/copilot-pull-request-reviewer`
- `dynamic/dependabot/dependabot-updates`
- `dynamic/agents/anthropic-code-agent`

**There is no `dynamic/github-code-scanning/codeql`.** CodeQL "default setup" registers exactly such a dynamic workflow when enabled, so its absence — while four *other* dynamic entries prove the listing does surface dynamic workflows — is the positive control that makes this a reading rather than an empty result.

**Therefore case 1 holds: CodeQL was never set up here.** The badge is false.

## Ruling — remove the badge

Delete the CodeQL badge line from `README.md` (line 11 on `origin/main` @ `e52fac0`, verified present today). This is enforce-or-remove on a declared-but-unenforced claim, on the most-read page in the repo — the card quotes this repo's own prior finding on why that direction is the dangerous one:

> *A doc that understates a gate is annoying; a doc that advertises a guardrail the CI does not have is worse than no doc, because people make size decisions believing something will stop them.*

⛔ **Do NOT add a CodeQL workflow.** Whether this repo *wants* code scanning is a separate product/security decision, maintainer-floor, and ⛔ must not be back-derived from a stale badge. If you think it should have one, say so in the report — ⛔ do not implement it.

## ⚠️ One accuracy trap — the repo is not unscanned

`.github/workflows/secret-scan.yml` ("Secret Scanning") **is** registered and active. ⛔ Do not write a changeset, commit message, PR body or code comment claiming the repo has "no security scanning" — it has secret scanning, just not CodeQL. Overstating the hole is the same class of error as the badge itself.

## Scope

`README.md` only, and within it only the CodeQL badge line. ⛔ Do not touch the other five badges (License, CI, TypeScript, React, Tailwind) — the CI badge points at `ci.yml`, which **is** registered and active.

Worth one line in the report, ⛔ not an edit: the badge block is **unpinned by construction** — the `ci-cd-pipeline.md` inventory pins cover `content/docs/guide/ci-cd-pipeline.md`, not the README, so it can drift again. If a cheap mechanical pin is obvious to you, **report it as a finding**; adding a new gate is out of this card's scope.

## Gates

Hand-derived (objectui has no `dispatch-gates.mjs`); re-derive against your actual diff. A README-only change should need Lint and the docs/link checks (`Check Links` / `Docs Links`) at most — **verify rather than assume**, since `README.md` is a package-adjacent doc and the changeset-presence rule may treat it specially. Judge changeset vs `skip-changeset` against the repo's own rule and **state which and why**.

## ACCEPT — PR #5963. ⛔ Landing HELD, on an unresolved landing-path question, ⛔ not on anything wrong with this PR.

Reviewer of record: `domain:devx` @ objectui seat (#5748), round **R6**, PM session `session_019b5UBNMtTzKbVtZZGvFuxe`. **Verified against the PR's own diff, file list and check runs on GitHub — ⛔ not against the report's self-description.**

### Checklist

| item | reading |
|:--|:--|
| PR shape | draft ✅ · base `main` ✅ · body first line `Fixes #5408` ✅ |
| scope | **1 file, 1 deletion, 0 additions** — matches the declared `README.md`-only surface exactly |
| the diff itself | read directly: removes precisely the CodeQL badge line. The five sibling badges (License, CI, TypeScript, React, Tailwind) are **byte-untouched**, verified in the diff context lines, ⛔ not taken on trust |
| ruling honoured | ⛔ no CodeQL workflow added; ⛔ `secret-scan.yml` untouched; ⛔ the fork was not re-investigated |
| CI | **19 checks: 16 success, 3 skipped, 0 failed.** `Doc Snippet Type Check` was `in_progress` at report time and converged green at 09:15:17 — re-read by name before this verdict, ⛔ not inferred from the aggregate |
| changeset | none added, none owed — the dev **ran** `check-changeset-presence.mjs` rather than asserting it, and `Changeset Declaration` + `Changeset Fixed Group Check` both pass on CI |
| report | arrived at draft-PR time with the `<!-- os-dev-report -->` marker ✅ |

### Reviewer's note on what the green actually proves

Most of the test jobs completed in ~11 seconds — they are path-filtered no-ops for a README-only diff. **⛔ Their green is not evidence about this change**, and I am not counting it as such. The evidence that carries this PR is the diff being a single deleted line, plus the workflow-registry reading that establishes the badge was false. Recording it so a later reader does not mistake a fast full-green for a broad one.

### The one thing the dev got right that a weaker run would have missed

It resisted the obvious overreach. Deleting a "security scan" badge invites the follow-on "so let me add CodeQL" — that is a maintainer-floor decision, and it stayed out. It also refused the opposite overstatement: the PR body explicitly records that `secret-scan.yml` **is** active, so the repo is not described as unscanned. Both directions of the false-claim error were avoided.

### Deviation — filed findings were missing their label; PM completed it

`out_of_scope_findings` were genuinely filed, unassigned, back-linked to #5408 and independently measured — I read both rather than trusting the report:

- **#5964** — `CONTRIBUTING.md` lists CodeQL under "Security Scans".
- **#5965** — `packages/vscode-extension/SUMMARY.md` claims 「CodeQL扫描通过」. Strictly worse than the badge: it asserts a specific *run outcome* for a scan that has never existed.

⚠️ Neither carried the `finding` label — #5965's own body even says *"Flagging as `finding`"* while the label was absent. **PM added `finding` to both.** Minor, but a naked card and a `finding` card enter triage by different routes, and the dev's filing duty includes the label. Grading is the triage seat's, ⛔ not mine.

Both are the same defect class as this card, so the class is **not** closed by this PR — two more false CodeQL claims remain on `main`.

### ⛔ Why this is not being landed now

Path-fork check run **before** touching ready/enqueue, against the PR's actual file list: `README.md` is **not** a governed surface (`docs/adr/**`, `.claude/**`, `skills/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`). So this PR is *eligible* for ready → landing, and every check is green.

It is held anyway, because **objectui's sanctioned landing path is unresolved and this seat will not pick one unilaterally.** The skill names the merge queue as the only sanctioned route and ⛔ forbids out-of-queue `--auto` merges; #4986 records that this repo's merge queue has never produced a single `merge_group` build. The previous seat landed six PRs by direct merge instead and flagged it twice without an answer. This round verified that claim rather than inheriting it: **PR #5960's `merged_by` is `os-warren`** — the PM session itself, ⛔ not `github-merge-queue[bot]` — so the bypass is real and repeated, not a misremembering.

Put to the maintainer in the live session; **this PR waits for that ruling.** ⛔ It is not blocked on any defect, and ⛔ nothing further is required of the dev.

## ⚠️ Correction: this card's dispatch comment contains a false claim — `secret-scan.yml` is not on `main`

Posted by the `domain:devx` @ objectui execution PM seat (#5748, PM session `session_019b5UBNMtTzKbVtZZGvFuxe`). This card is **merged** (PR #5963) and nothing shipped wrong — the claim is in the dispatch comment, **not in the diff**. Correcting it here so it is not quoted forward.

### The claim

This card's dispatch states that `.github/workflows/secret-scan.yml` ("Secret Scanning") **is registered and active**. Measured on `origin/main` during #5964 / PR #6065: **it is not on `main`, and never has been.**

```
git cat-file -e origin/main:.github/workflows/secret-scan.yml   -> does not exist
git cat-file -e origin/main:.github/workflows/ci.yml            -> resolves        (control)
git log origin/main --full-history -- *secret-scan.yml          -> empty
```

It was added and then deleted (`041dfb107`) on the unmerged branch `copilot/add-github-workflows` — neither commit an ancestor of `main`. Its only three runs ever were on that PR branch in Jan 2026, and **all three concluded `failure`**.

### Why it matters, and it is not academic

The claim propagated. **#5964** inherited it and went one step further: it instructed the implementer to write "the registered secret-scan workflow" into `CONTRIBUTING.md` as the *corrected* text — which would have replaced one false security-tooling claim with another, in the very card that exists to remove such claims. It was caught only because that dev checked the replacement against `main` rather than trusting the card.

### Root cause

The registry says `active` for workflows that are not on `main`, and omits some that are. That is not specific to `secret-scan.yml` — `changeset-check.yml`, `validate-docs-links.yml` and both `proto-5395-*.yml` are in the same state, while `half-state-patrol.yml` and `hook-selftests.yml` are on disk but missing from the listing. **Registry state `active` is not evidence a workflow exists or runs**, in either direction.

Filed as **#6069**.

### What still stands

The substance of this card's finding is unaffected: **no CodeQL scan runs on this repository.** That was verified independently and again during #5964 (`find .github -iname '*codeql*'` empty against `-iname '*lint*'` resolving `lint.yml`; enumeration surfacing four `dynamic/*` entries but no `dynamic/github-code-scanning/codeql`). Only the "what runs instead" half was wrong.

For the record, the scan that **is** verified to run here is **Dependabot** — registered and active as `dynamic/dependabot/dependabot-updates`, with `.github/dependabot.yml` present on `main` and weekly npm + Actions update PRs actually landing. PR #6065 corrects `CONTRIBUTING.md` to say that, plus an explicit sentence that no static-analysis scanning exists, so the false inference cannot re-form from a bare omission.
